notes: Matching was by anchor position and rule; I un-paired and re-paired mispaired units (for example, A and B anchoring different sentences of the same bullet) before counting. Main disagreements and resolutions: (1) actor: in the faculty/staff AUP, B coded ta-staff where A coded all; resolved to all because the document addresses faculty and staff together; in the undergraduate policy admin vs all was settled by who the sentence binds (scope and cross-policy statements all; the colleges' own purpose statements admin). (2) phase: general vs during-work and course-start vs before-course; resolved by whether the rule governs doing the work, communicating expectations, or setting up the policy. (3) modality: must vs should for 'belongs on the syllabus' and the sample disclosure line (kept the passage's own wording, should), and informs vs must for institutional 'will' commitments (must). (4) policy_type: the main splits were P04 vs P83 (instructor decides), P06 vs P107 (silent-syllabus fallback vs written permission), P61 vs P24 (definition of disclosure), P40 vs P26, P56 vs P116/P61/P65 for framework sentences, P05 vs P01 for the Assistive Only template ban, and P19 vs UNCOVERED for AI output represented as own work (kept UNCOVERED). (5) unit_stance: A tended to code obligations and safe harbors as neutral/permit where B coded restrict/prohibit; resolved by whether the sentence limits AI use itself. Only-one-coder units: B coded many more discrete sentences (rationale sentences, individual assessment-design bullets, definitions); every one was checked against the source and kept except 4 dropped:  one repeated UG 4 sample sentence (A), two headings or repeated instructions (B), and one template heading (B). Stance: ugai and resources agreed (delegates); AUP resolved to permit (A had delegates). Coder-written fit_notes and uncovered_notes were merged, none dropped.
